mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or inflation-adjusted returns remain flat.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS (monthly payrolls) coincides with stronger consumer confidence, which amplifies corporate hiring intentions and drives S&P 500 forward returns over a 60-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 140,000 in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative when PAYEMS crosses above 140,000 in non-recessionary conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in household demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending demand shortfall, which precedes a short-term S&P 500 pullback over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by 10% while INDPRO decreases by 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when the HOUST-INDPRO pattern occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial supply as measured by INDPRO (monthly index) below 110 for two consecutive months triggers a supply-side risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite INDPRO remaining below 110 for >30 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it indicates a labor market softening that reduces the real discount rate, supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for >6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) above 150,000 combined with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a strong labor market, which drives optimism into equities and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 150,000 and UNRATE < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns miss the predicted positive move when both indicators occur in a non-stagflationary environment.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 208 over the last 3 months), the S&P 500 anticipates future rate hikes, generating negative forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when CPIAUCSL remains elevated for >90 days.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (INDPRO < 110 for 4 months) creates persistent supply-side uncertainty, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are non-negative when the INDPRO condition persists beyond 6 months.
